title: I left my 13-year career at Google to work in sustainability. It wasn't an easy choice, but my values had changed.
summary:
That path led me first to consulting and then to Google, where I spent more than 13 years before leaving to pursue work in sustainability.
In 2012, I was invited to a friend's birthday dinner, where I was seated opposite a guy working at Google.
A year later, I applied for a full-time role working with DoubleClick for Publishers, now part of Google Ad Manager.
While still at Google, I looked into which universities offered degrees in sustainability and came across a program at Harvard.
In December 2025, I resigned from GoogleI pursued my master's degree in sustainable studies at Harvard online while working at Google.

title: Singapore is cloaked in a fire-related haze. Here's what it looks like
summary:
Singapore, the Southeast Asian financial hub known for its futuristic skyline, has been blanketed by milky haze as smoke from fires in neighboring Indonesia drifts across the region.
The haze has affected Singapore for weeks, with conditions deteriorating in recent days.
The pollution has disrupted flights, shut down outdoor sports facilities, and prompted organizers to call off a major running event.
On Friday, air quality in parts of Singapore reached "very unhealthy" levels, with pollution readings hitting their highest point this year.
Here's what the haze looks like across the city.

title: Severe drought declared in parts of southern England
summary:
South East Water's operations director Douglas Whitfield said standpipes remained part of the company's drought plan but were unlikely to be needed.
Whitfield said South East Water, which supplies more than two million customers, said 92 repair crews were out across Sussex and Kent tackling leaks to minimise loss from the network.
Wessex Water, which supplies customers from Wimbleball, introduced its first hosepipe ban in 50 years in August and said the restrictions would remain in place for the foreseeable future.

title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms
summary:
Brazil's government says deforestation rates in the country's Amazon and savanna regions have fallen to record lows ahead of a presidential election run-off in which the rainforest's future is a key issue.
Left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, when he assumed office three years ago, pledged to end deforestation by 2030 in the Amazon.
Flavio is expected to continue his father's policies if he wins, though he has pledged to fight organised crime in the Amazon.
The fall in the Cerrado, Brazil's savanna region, was 23.8%.
The Amazon rainforest - the world's largest - is a crucial buffer in the global fight against climate change and 60% of it is located in Brazil.

title: 'Nowhere to escape' - Indonesians share footage of orange haze blanketing towns
summary:
A thick orange smog has descended on the Indonesian city of Palangka Raya.
Witnesses captured videos of the haze washing over the Kalimantan region not far from where wildfires continue to burn.
The ISPU air pollution index exceeded 1,200, according to data from the national environment ministry, four times higher than the "hazardous" level of 300 on Wednesday.
Toxic smog is choking millions across Indonesia, Singapore and Malaysia, with authorities partly blaming the agricultural clearing method known as "slash and burn" for compounding the intense haze.

title: What Should Exterior Insulation Do Beyond Thermal Performance?
summary:
Yet Exterior Insulation Finishing Systems (EIFS) are still frequently reduced to insulation thermal conductivity, thickness, external envelope U-values and regulatory compliance.
In new construction, continuous exterior insulation is automatically designed around the structure from the outset, helping to eliminate thermal bridges.
Exterior insulation systems naturally extend this philosophy because they ultimately form part of the finished façade.
For architects and designers, the art lies in creating without treating exterior insulation as a constraint on form or finish.
Its exterior insulation portfolio includes EIFS Alpha (EPS/Graphite EPS Insulation), EIFS Perma (Mineral Wool Insulation) and EIFS Nova (Phenolic Foam Insulation) alongside Direct Applied Exterior Finishing Systems (DEFS), XFS Beta (Acrylic basecoat) and XFS Delta (Cementitious basecoat), providing solutions for conventional on-site construction as well as off-site construction for both traditional and steel-frame structures.

title: Catherine says nature can help children's emotional growth
summary:
The Princess of Wales has launched a project promoting the use of nature to help develop young children's social and emotional development.
This is the latest stage in Catherine's campaign to improve the status of early years education and to find ways to improve children's wellbeing.
She says that research has shown "just how important nature is for our psychological and physiological wellbeing".
This faith in nature is now being applied to her early years project - the Royal Foundation Centre for Early Childhood.
A new photograph of Catherine taken on Thursday in Cornwall by Josh Shinner has been released to accompany the project.

title: Restoring nature is key to a more resilient future
summary:
Evidence shows that under the right conditions, positive change can cross a tipping point threshold and become self-reinforcing, making a safer, more resilient future not just possible, but inevitable.
The question is: How can we accelerate the actions needed to trigger those tipping points and accelerate the transition?
Positive tipping points and the opportunity for transformational changeIn environmental terms, we often think about tipping points in terms of the threats they pose to vital ecosystems, such as coral reefs or the Amazon rainforest, where constant damage risks compounding and becoming increasingly impossible to reverse.
However, these tipping point dynamics can also work in our favour.
Triggering tipping points in those systems would see them rapidly transform for the better and reduce harm to the climate and nature.
